description:
Hosted data residency enforcement is an enterprise security & compliance foundation project to ensure customer traffic and stored artifacts (prompts, completions, embeddings payloads, request metadata, logs, and optional persistence features) remain within an approved cloud region boundary. The project adds region pinning controls at the org/project/workspace level and enforces them at runtime across the request path (API gateway/control plane policy evaluation, routing, and any storage/logging side effects). When a violation occurs (e.g., request hits a non-approved region due to misconfiguration, fallback routing, or SDK-specified region mismatch), the platform must return clear, actionable error messaging and emit audit events for compliance evidence.

Goals:
- Introduce region pinning configuration (e.g., allowed_regions=["eu-west"], pinned_region="eu-west") for Hosted and Dedicated; define behavior for Private/VPC deployments.
- Enforce residency at request admission (before model execution) and for downstream writes (audit logs, traces, object storage, analytics pipelines).
- Provide deterministic routing behavior when region pinning is enabled (no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed and recorded).
- Implement clear error responses (HTTP status + machine-readable error codes) with remediation guidance.
- Add observability: metrics, dashboards, alerting, and audit log entries for residency decisions/violations.
- Provide a migration/rollout plan (feature flags, canary, customer comms) and documentation for Support/Sales.

Non-goals (initial release):
- Full data lifecycle residency for all historical datasets (handled via separate retention/migration initiatives).
- Automatic region migration of existing customer artifacts.

Primary stakeholders:
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments).
- Engineering: Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing), Vikram Singh (Data Plane).
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin; GRC/evidence: Olga Petrov.
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (alerts, incident readiness).
- DevEx/Docs: updates to docs site and SDK guidance; Support & CS for escalation playbooks.

High-level timeline (illustrative):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements, threat model, ADRs, API contract, error code taxonomy.
- Phase 1 (3–6 weeks): implementation across config/policy service, gateway enforcement, routing constraints, audit/metrics.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): console UX + docs/SDK updates, canary rollout, customer pilots.
- Phase 3 (GA): default-on for enterprise plans, support playbooks, compliance evidence packaging.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence PRD/design spec + ADRs; runbooks and support documentation.
- Linear initiative and execution tickets.
- GitHub PRs implementing policy evaluation, routing changes, logging/auditing, SDK/docs updates, terraform defaults.
- Slack coordination threads, incident-readiness discussions, and support escalations.
- Customer-facing artifacts (sales/security calls, email threads, CRM notes) reflecting enterprise rollout and requirements.

files.description: High-level overview of the residency enforcement program: definitions (what counts as in-scope data), supported regions, customer-facing guarantees by product tier, and links to implementation specs/runbooks.
PRD covering user stories (security admins, platform engineers), configuration model (org/project pinning), success metrics, rollout plan, and pricing/packaging assumptions for enterprise controls.
End-to-end system design: control plane config, policy evaluation points, routing constraints, error contracts, audit events, and compatibility with Dedicated/Private.
ADR choosing the policy model (pinned_region vs allowed_regions), precedence rules, defaults, and how policies are stored/validated.
ADR documenting enforcement location(s) (API gateway vs router vs model runtime) and rationale (latency, correctness, failure modes).
Standardized error codes and HTTP mappings for residency violations (e.g., RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH), including examples, remediation tips, and SDK guidance.
Specification for audit log events emitted for residency decisions and violations: fields, retention, SIEM export considerations, and evidence collection guidance.
Service doc for the policy evaluator/control plane component: APIs, caching, failure behavior, and how residency policies are evaluated and propagated.
Operational runbook for handling spikes in residency violation errors: dashboards to check, common causes (misconfig, fallback), mitigation steps, and comms templates.
Dashboards and alert definitions: violation rate by region/customer, policy-evaluator error rates, routing fallback counters, and SLO impact monitoring.
Process for granting/recording exceptions (temporary cross-region allowance), required approvals (Security/GRC), audit requirements, and expiry enforcement.
Support/CS playbook: triage checklist, what logs to request, how to identify configuration mismatches, and when to engage SRE/Security.
PM initiative tracking milestones (design signoff, beta, GA), cross-team dependencies, customer pilots, and release criteria.
Engineering ticket for implementing policy storage schema, validation rules, and admin APIs for region pinning.
Implement request admission checks at the API gateway; return standardized error codes/messages; ensure checks run before model execution.

Emit audit log events for allow/deny decisions; ensure export pipeline includes required fields; align with GRC evidence needs.
